questions.question: What is the execution order of a basic for loop?

options.value: Initialize, test, body, update, test again
Test once, repeat body without updates

questions.explanation: Initialization happens once, then the test/body/update cycle repeats.

questions.question: How often does the initialization clause normally execute?

options.value: Once when the loop is entered

questions.explanation: Initialization sets up the loop before the first condition test.

questions.question: When does the update clause normally run?

options.value: Only when the first test is false

questions.explanation: The update precedes the next condition test.

questions.question: How many times does for (int i = 0; i < 0; i++) execute its body?
What is the scope of i declared in for (int i = 0; ...)?
questions.explanation: A loop-local variable is not available after the loop finishes.

questions.question: Which loop visits 0 through 4?
questions.explanation: The exclusive bound 5 yields exactly five indices.

questions.question: Which update is appropriate for a countdown with condition i > 0?
questions.explanation: Decrement moves a positive counter toward zero.

questions.question: Can a for loop be rewritten as a while loop with equivalent control flow?

options.value: No, for loops use a different arithmetic system
Only if there are no variables
Yes, with corresponding initialization, condition, and update

questions.explanation: Both structures can express the same repetitive algorithm when updates are placed correctly.

How many body executions?
for (int i = 0; i < 3; i++) { work(); }
questions.explanation: The visited values are 0 through n - 1.

questions.question:
How many body executions?
for (int i = 1; i <= 3; i += 2) { work(); }
questions.explanation: The loop visits the odd integers from 1 through this odd inclusive bound.
